stability: Every entry in `outputs` is stable API: labels, basenames, and the field names/nesting shown in each example. Removing or renaming any of them is a breaking change and requires a TOOL_VERSION bump plus a changelog note here. Files NOT listed here (per-fixed-chunk segments/ VAD turns, dynamic/ speech groups, per-chunk transcripts/transcript_{n}.json and embeddings/embeddings_{n}.json intermediates, workflow_params.json, converted audio under media_processing/, resampled/, clipped/) are internal and may change or vanish without notice. `description` is one line by design — it is joined verbatim into each get_job_status outputs[] entry as `desc`.

transcript.description: Speaker-labelled sentence + word transcript — use for: subtitle/text projections, speaker-tagged quotes, seeking by sentence; words[] joins sentences via word_id_range
transcript.notes: Written at {prefix}/transcripts/final_transcript.json (transcripts/ subdirectory, not the prefix root). Times are seconds from audio start. speaker_id is SPEAKER_NN or null when no speaker could be assigned; confidence and probability may be null. word_id_range is the inclusive [first, last] id span into the flat words[] array; a sentence with no word timestamps has an inverted range. overlap_spans (added 2026-08-26) are cross-talk ranges: VAD speech turns in which >=2 speakers were simultaneously active for at least one frame — turn-granular, not frame-exact; [] when none. Derive per-sentence flags by time-join against sentences[]. word_timing_source (added 2026-09-16) records word-timestamp provenance: 'aligned:<lang>' (forced alignment, precise), 'aligned:en_fallback' (English-model alignment on a language without its own model - degraded), or 'whisper_native' (no alignment; coarse). speech_spans (added 2026-09-16) are word-tight [start,end] spans per sentence, split at intra-sentence pauses >0.5s when alignment ran; with whisper_native timing the sentence span is returned unsplit (coarse boundaries must not cut speech). Prefer speech_spans over sentence start/end for speech-activity uses (silence between spans is real). overlap_segments (2026-09-18): identity-resolved cross-talk spans {start, end, speakers:[two SPEAKER_NN]} — records the second voice sentences[] structurally misses (one speaker per instant). Evidence, not verdict: identity mapping measured 81% precise on the development corpus (zh 56-69%), ~1 in 5 segments may name one wrong speaker — prefer aggregate uses over per-instance claims; [] when none resolved. pad_resolution (added 2026-10-12, optional per word): provenance of a word whose Whisper timestamp fell in a synthetic inter-group concatenation pad — 'pad_moved' (relocated to the owning speech group by the resolution ladder), 'pad_unresolved' (kept, clamped — the evidence could not adjudicate: no aligner, probe abstention, or a support tie within the margin), or 'pad_rehomed' (re-homed next to its sentence-mates after sentence assembly). Absent on words whose timestamps were observed in place; flagged timings are reconstructed, not observed. Hallucinated pad words with no acoustic support are dropped and never appear.

caption.description: Speaker-tagged WebVTT captions (Netflix-style line/duration limits) — use as <track> subtitles against the proxy
caption.notes: Written at {prefix}/transcripts/final_transcript.vtt. A WEBVTT header then cues of `HH:MM:SS.mmm --> HH:MM:SS.mmm` followed by `<v SPEAKER_NN>text` — the voice tag carries the transcript's speaker_id (UNKNOWN when unassigned). Netflix Timed Text limits: max 42 chars/line, 2 lines/cue, 7 s max cue duration, >=83 ms gap between cues; long sentences are split into multiple cues at word boundaries, never truncated.

speaker-manifest.description: Per-speaker WAV index (durations, segment counts, compact time_map) — use for speaker lanes/turns and for resolving speaker-audio keys
speaker-manifest.notes: Written at {prefix}/speakers/speaker_manifest.json. `speakers` is an object keyed by SPEAKER_NN — ids can be non-contiguous (a speaker with no valid audio regions writes no WAV and no entry). channel_mode is `aligned` or `compact`; in compact mode each speaker entry adds duration_sec and time_map ([{original_start, original_end, compact_start, compact_end}], seconds) and the top level adds compact_gap_sec. This file is the index for the speaker-audio prefix.

global-speakers.description: Speaker clustering result (centroid models, sentence→speaker map, diagnostics) — use for cross-run speaker matching or clustering QC; the transcript already carries per-sentence speaker_id
global-speakers.notes: Written at {prefix}/embeddings/global_speakers.json. sentence_speakers keys are `{dyn_chunk_idx}:{sentence_idx}` — internal chunk-local ids; join speakers via the transcript's per-sentence speaker_id instead. Values can be UNKNOWN. speaker_models[*].embedding is the 256-dim WeSpeaker centroid (truncated here); diarization segments are merged same-speaker turns. k_sweep_log holds one diagnostic record per candidate K — diagnostics internals, kept shallow here because their shape may deepen. f0_* fields (2026-09-23) are per-cluster voice-pitch STATISTICS (median/IQR of per-sentence F0 medians, voiced-frame ratio) — evidence for downstream voice-to-face compatibility matching, never a gender verdict (thresholds and the abstention band belong to the consumer); absent when nothing voiced or on pre-F0 runs.

usage.description: Per-state durations and estimated cost, including the media-processing child run — use for reporting what this run cost
usage.notes: Costs are us-east-1 arm64 estimates, not billing data. total_estimated_cost covers parent + child. media_processing is null when the source needed no format conversion; its states[] entries share the parent states[] entry shape. The synthetic `Usage tracking` self-entry estimates its own not-yet-finished invocation and omits retried/incomplete.

speaker-audio.description: Per-speaker WAV channels (source-timeline aligned or compact) — use for voice ID, sentiment, or voice-cloning reference audio; resolve exact keys from speaker-manifest
speaker-audio.notes: Files are {prefix}/speakers/SPEAKER_{NN}.wav — mono int16 at the source's native sample rate. They are not individually enumerated in outputs[] (speaker ids can be non-contiguous); speaker_manifest.json in the same prefix is the index. Present only when speaker_channels=true and at least one speaker produced audio. `aligned` mode WAVs share the source timeline (silence elsewhere); `compact` mode holds only the speaker's speech — map times back via the manifest's time_map.
